**Triage — R+118.** `bug` · `priority:p2` · `pm:queue` · `domain:ui`. ⛔ Not claimed, not dispatched.

## Verification (`origin/main` `ac8d523`)

Confirmed at the declaration site. `packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts:5667` opens

```ts
export function createObjectStackAdapter<T = unknown>(config: { … }): DataSource<T> {
```

so the declared return really is `DataSource<T>`, and everything the adapter carries beyond the `DataSource` interface is unreachable through this entry point in TypeScript. The card names `setSystemCapabilities` as an example and the JSDoc immediately above the config bag (`:5677`, `[ADR-0066] See {@link ObjectStackAdapter.setSystemCapabilities}`) points at exactly that method — so the file's own doc comment refers the reader to an API its declared return type hides.

## What I did NOT measure

⛔ I did not enumerate which members are lost, and I did not check whether the widening is safe. Two things decide that and neither is answered here:

1. **Is `ObjectStackAdapter` exported?** If the class is not part of the public surface, widening the return type to it exports the class by implication — a bigger change than it looks, and Clause ② territory.
2. **Is the narrow return deliberate?** A `DataSource<T>` return is exactly how you keep an adapter swappable. If that was the intent, the defect is the **README and the JSDoc promising more**, and the fix is prose, not types.

⇒ Stop-condition: answer those two from the code *before* choosing a diff, and put both answers in the report. If the class turns out to be intentionally private, ⛔ do not export it to make the doc true — say so and let the docs change instead.

## Anchoring

`domain:ui` — `packages/data-objectstack` is a published library ⇒ the objectui three-stream split routes it to `domain:ui`. ⛔ Not `domain:spec`; no `packages/types` contract moves under either fix.

## Why `p2`

A published entry point under-declares its own API and the file's own JSDoc points at the hidden half — but nothing misbehaves at runtime and there is a documented workaround (name the class directly). Real, bounded, not urgent.

**Claim** — session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`, branch `claude/issue-7323-adapter-return-type`, dispatched by the `domain:ui` PM seat. No earlier claim comment on this thread (the only prior comment is the R+118 triage, which says unclaimed).

Clause-②: yes

Why `yes`: the branch I am taking is option **A** — widen the declared return of the published factory `createObjectStackAdapter` from the shared `DataSource` interface to the concrete adapter type. That enlarges the declared public surface reachable through a published entry point (`packages/data-objectstack/dist/index.d.ts`): members that today are hidden behind the narrow return — `getClient`, `getCacheStats`, `invalidateCache`, `clearCache`, `getConnectionState`, `isConnected`, `onConnectionStateChange`, `onBatchProgress`, `setSystemCapabilities` — become reachable from the factory. The declaration limb is path-independent and judged from the card's content, so it is `yes` regardless of how few files the diff touches. `needs:contract-review` goes on both carriers (this card and the PR).

Answers to the triage's two stop-condition questions, from the code on today's `origin/main` (`e17605309`), recorded here because they decide the shape:

- **Q1 — is `ObjectStackAdapter` exported from the public entry?** Yes, already. `packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts:2148` reads `export class ObjectStackAdapter` and `tsup.config.ts` has exactly one entry, `src/index.ts`, so the class is in the shipped `dist/index.d.ts`. Two pin tests already assert the exported spelling in source (`cloud-surface-retired-4152.pin.test.ts:114`, `v3-deep-integration-retired-4241.pin.test.ts:135`), and `apps/console/src/dataSource.ts:14` re-exports it by name. So widening the return does **not** export the class by implication — there is no new class export in the diff. That removes the triage's specific worry, though not the declaration itself.
- **Q2 — is the narrow return deliberate?** No evidence that it is, and two pieces of evidence that it is not. (a) Commit `a5d817061` added `autoReconnect` / `maxReconnectAttempts` / `reconnectDelay` to the *factory's own config bag* while leaving the members that observe those features off the factory's declared return — the same change configured a feature it made unobservable through its own entry point. (b) The factory's JSDoc, added by `41b7ce3ce`, points the reader at `ObjectStackAdapter.setSystemCapabilities`, a member its declared return hides. No comment, ADR or test anywhere pins the return as `DataSource`; there is no `Equal` assertion on it and no swappability note. The README documents the class constructor as public and today has to tell readers to hold the class instead.

Full verification readouts land in the report comment (first line `os-dev-report`) when the draft PR is up.

## Two corrections to the dispatch brief

1. **The member count is 9, not 4+4.** The brief says four members fail and lists four more as documented-but-unmeasured. Measured against the shipped `dist`, all nine fail together with TS2339, `setSystemCapabilities` included — the one the file's own JSDoc points at. The brief's framing implies two tiers; there is only one.
2. **The line anchor moved, as the brief predicted.** `packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts:5667` was correct at triage time and correct at dispatch; the declaration site on `origin/main` `e17605309` is `:5680`, and `export class ObjectStackAdapter` is at `:2148`. Re-derived rather than trusted, per the brief's own warning.

Nothing else in the brief was wrong. The fork was the right question to ask: Q1 came back "already exported", which is what makes this a one-line fix rather than a public-surface expansion by implication, and Q2 came back "not deliberate", which is what keeps it out of the docs-only branch. The `needs:contract-review` gate is still warranted on the content limb, and the PR names the one direction in which the change is not purely additive (a hand-written structural stand-in can no longer satisfy the factory's return, because the widened type is a class with private members).
